lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 5: kubectl essentials
lesson.description: Imperative vs declarative kubectl, YAML from dry-run, apply, diff, explain, edit and patch, every -o output format, and label selectors, all tested on kind.
lesson.tested: Every command ran on a kind v0.33.0 cluster (node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2) on 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Keep manifests in files and use diff then apply. Use dry-run to write YAML, explain to read fields, -o to shape output, and labels with -l to pick objects.

cheatsheet.intro: The three ways to manage objects, the lab commands, and the selector forms from Lesson 5.

boards.title: Three ways to manage an object
boards.hint: the object management page, as the lesson states it

rows.name: Imperative commands
rows.role: Act on live objects with flags. Fast, and good for learning and one-off tasks. They leave no file, so there is nothing to review, nothing in Git, and no record except the cluster itself.

rows.name: Imperative object configuration
rows.role: A file, and a verb you choose. You can review the file, and you must pick the right verb. `create` fails if the object exists. `replace` overwrites the whole object with your file, dropping anything that was set elsewhere.

rows.name: Declarative object configuration
rows.role: You describe what you want and kubectl works out whether to create or patch each object. Pair it with `kubectl diff` to see the change first. This is how the rest of the series works.

boards.note: Manage each object with only one technique. Mixing them on the same object gives results the docs call undefined. The lab shows a mild version: an edit made outside the file lasts only until the next apply.

boards.title: Selectors
boards.hint: equality-based and set-based, from the labels page as the lesson states it

rows.name: Equality
rows.role: `=`, `==` or `!=`. A comma between requirements means AND. There is no OR operator.

rows.name: Inequality
rows.role: The docs spell this out: inequality matches objects without the key too.

rows.name: Set-based
rows.role: `in`, `notin`, and plain existence (`key` or `!key`). `in (a,b)` is how you match either value. Use single quotes so the shell leaves the parentheses and `!` alone.
rows.where: `environment in (dev,prod)` matched the three shop Pods. `!environment` matched scratch

steps.title: Life of Pod web
steps.hint: generate, diff, apply, then watch a live edit lose

items.what: `--dry-run=client -o yaml` builds the object locally and sends nothing. The lesson's YAML has labels `app.kubernetes.io/name: web` and `tier: frontend`, image `nginx:1.29-alpine`, and `containerPort: 80`. Redirect it with `> web.yaml`. You can delete `resources: {}` and `status: {}`.
The first run prints `pod/web created`. The second prints `pod/web unchanged`. apply is idempotent.

After you add `environment: dev` under labels, the diff shows that added line. Exit code `0` means no differences, `1` means differences, and more than `1` means an error. The lesson checked `0` before the edit and `1` after it. apply then prints `pod/web configured`.
Opens the live object in `KUBE_EDITOR` or `EDITOR`. The lesson changed `environment` from `dev` to `test`. The next `kubectl apply -f web.yaml` put `dev` back, because that field belongs to the file.
`owner=me` is a label the file never mentions. The next apply prints `pod/web unchanged` and `--show-labels` still lists `owner=me`.

steps.note: apply remembers the last applied object in the annotation `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration`. A JSON merge patch can change one label. Patching the container port is refused: most of a running Pod's spec is fixed. The Pods page lists the fields a Pod update may change.

homework.intro: Use the kind cluster and the namespace `k8s-from-zero` from part 4. The lesson's node is `k8s-ep04-control-plane`, so node names and Pod UIDs on yours will differ. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: Name the three object-management techniques, and say which one the rest of the series uses.
exercises.a: Imperative commands (flags on live objects), imperative object configuration (a file plus a verb you choose: `create -f`, `replace -f`, `delete -f`), and declarative object configuration (`kubectl apply -f` on files or directories). The series uses declarative configuration, paired with `kubectl diff`.

exercises.q: What rule does the object management page add about mixing techniques?
exercises.a: Manage each object with only one technique. Mixing them on the same object gives results the docs call undefined.

exercises.q: What does kubectl itself store, and what does `-v=6` add?
exercises.a: kubectl stores nothing. Every command becomes one or more HTTPS requests to the kube-apiserver. `-v=6` raises the log level enough to print each request. The lesson's line shows verb GET, the URL under `/api/v1/namespaces/k8s-from-zero/pods`, and status `200 OK`.
`--dry-run=client` builds the object locally and sends nothing. `--dry-run=server` sends the request through the API server's full validation and admission checks but stores nothing.

exercises.q: What three exit codes does `kubectl diff` use?
exercises.a: `0` means no differences, `1` means differences, and more than `1` means an error. The lesson checked `0` before the edit and `1` after it.

exercises.q: In a label selector, what does a comma mean, and which objects does `!=` match besides the ones with a different value?
exercises.a: A comma means AND, and there is no OR operator. Inequality also matches objects that do not have the key. In the lab, `tier!=frontend` matched scratch, which has no `tier` label.

sections.title: Run this and explain
sections.hint: Run each command on your cluster, then answer.

exercises.q: Run `kubectl run quick --image=nginx:1.29-alpine -n k8s-from-zero`. What does the lesson print, and which technique is this?
exercises.a: `pod/quick created`. It is an imperative command: one line, no file left behind.

exercises.q: Run the `kubectl run web ... --dry-run=client -o yaml` command from step 2. Which labels does the lesson's YAML contain, and which two fields does the lesson say you can delete?
exercises.a: `app.kubernetes.io/name: web` and `tier: frontend`. You can delete `resources: {}` and `status: {}`. The image is `nginx:1.29-alpine` and `containerPort` is 80.

exercises.q: Apply `web.yaml` twice. What does each run print?
exercises.a: `pod/web created`, then `pod/web unchanged`. apply is idempotent.

exercises.q: Add `environment: dev` under `labels` and run `kubectl diff -f web.yaml`. What line does the lesson's diff add, and what is the exit code?
exercises.a: The added line is `environment: dev`. The exit code is `1`, which means differences. apply then prints `pod/web configured`.

exercises.q: Run `kubectl explain pod.spec.containers.imagePullPolicy`. Which three values does the lesson list, and when is the default `Always`?
exercises.a: `Always`, `IfNotPresent` and `Never`. The description in the lesson says the default is Always if the `:latest` tag is specified, or IfNotPresent otherwise. The field cannot be updated.

exercises.q: Apply `shop.yaml` and run the three equality selectors from the lesson (`tier=frontend`, `tier=frontend,environment=prod`, `tier!=frontend`). Which Pod names come back for each?
exercises.a: `tier=frontend` returns shop-web-dev and shop-web-prod. Adding `environment=prod` returns only shop-web-prod. `tier!=frontend` returns scratch and shop-api-prod.

exercises.q: Run `kubectl label pod scratch -n k8s-from-zero environment=dev`, then the same command with `environment=test` and no `--overwrite`. What error does the lesson print?
exercises.a: The first command prints `pod/scratch labeled`. The second prints `error: 'environment' already has a value (dev), and --overwrite is false`.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: You run `kubectl create -f web.yaml` for a Pod named `web` that already exists. What error does the lesson quote?
exercises.a: `Error from server (AlreadyExists): error when creating "web.yaml": pods "web" already exists`. `create` only creates. Use `apply` for files you keep changing.

exercises.q: You `kubectl edit` Pod web so `environment` is `test`, then `kubectl apply -f web.yaml` while the file still says `dev`. What does ENVIRONMENT show afterwards, and what happens to a label `owner=me` that the file never mentions?
exercises.a: apply prints `pod/web configured` and ENVIRONMENT is `dev` again, because the file owns that field. `owner=me` stays. The lesson's `--show-labels` line lists `app.kubernetes.io/name=web,environment=dev,owner=me,tier=frontend`.

exercises.q: You JSON-patch Pod web so container `web` has `containerPort` 8080. What does the API do?
exercises.a: It refuses the update. The lesson quotes: `The Pod "web" is invalid: spec: Forbidden: pod updates may not change fields other than` the image fields, `spec.activeDeadlineSeconds`, additions to `spec.tolerations`, and `spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds` in the case the lesson names. For anything else you replace the Pod.

exercises.q: You run `kubectl get pods -n k8s-from-zero -l tier=Frontend`. What does the lesson say comes back, and why?
exercises.a: Nothing. Values are case-sensitive, and the lesson says `-l tier=Frontend` found nothing. Check with `--show-labels` or `-L tier` first.

exercises.q: You are about to run `kubectl delete pods -n k8s-from-zero -l environment=dev`. What does the lesson tell you to run first, and which Pod did that selector delete in the lab?
exercises.a: Run `kubectl get pods -l ...` with the same selector first. In the lab the delete removed `shop-web-dev`. A later `kubectl delete -f shop.yaml` reports `NotFound` for that Pod and removes the rest.
